pairs.subject: data-access
pairs.evidence: src/lib/campaigns/store/campaigns.ts:178 The campaign mapper accepts unknown stored statuses through a type assertion, allowing corrupt vocabulary values to reach callers as valid domain records.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/campaigns/store/reports.ts:254 The plural history operation reads the collection once and groups results by report key instead of fetching each campaign's history separately.
src/lib/campaigns/store/local-docs.ts:220 The JSON path and predicate values are bound parameters; executable SQL shapes are selected from constant statements.
src/lib/campaigns/store/campaigns.ts:178 The mapper asserts enum membership without validating it or producing an explicit corruption outcome.

src/lib/campaigns/store/campaigns.ts:125 Same-millisecond snapshots receive random suffixes, yet readers use descending document IDs to select the newest snapshots, making their temporal order arbitrary.
src/lib/campaigns/store/campaigns.ts:93 The stale-set read precedes the atomic write batch, so concurrent replacements can both delete the old set and leave a union of their incoming campaigns.

pairs.evidence: src/lib/campaigns/connection.ts:93 Account updates overwrite an array derived from an earlier unguarded read, so concurrent connection changes can lose one another.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/campaigns/mutations.ts:285 The shift requests both campaign budgets together and associates the returned values by campaign ID.

pairs.evidence: src/lib/recaps/store.ts:49 Recap history is replaced from an unguarded prior read, allowing concurrent appends to lose history and a swallowed read failure to overwrite it.

techniques.evidence: src/app/api/projects/[id]/advice/route.ts:44 The handler performs ownership and input checks, then calls a named store operation rather than constructing a persistence query.
